question.problem:
Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by

$$
p_1(t)=3+2t, \qquad
	p_2(t)=-t+t^2.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242549/assets/9eca81c24ee88a63d1c5468160a118cb1e987793d5fdc8d2d7eaa317fadeda93.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14242549/assets/8c3fce8e9d7cc170ad66706e783c4a46ba0530c119b8b824a66d9b5850e62760.svg)

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =4\cdot (3+2t)+(-3)\cdot (-t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =12+8t+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =12+11t-3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
